title: Marisol, Grade 4: multilingual access and evidence gaps
practiceFocus: Language access, assessment validity and an evidence plan
languageContext: Spanish and English; language and literacy history require further review
narrative: Marisol is age 9 years, 10 months, in Grade 4. She uses Spanish with her family and English and Spanish at school. Her family describes detailed Spanish storytelling, an interest in science and persistent difficulty reading unfamiliar words in Spanish. She explains mathematical reasoning well with diagrams. She attended Spanish-medium school in Grades 1-2, with a four-month interruption during a school closure, and entered English-medium instruction in Grade 3. Prior literacy-instruction records are incomplete.

The current school documents regular attendance and scheduled ESOL instruction. The ESOL teacher reports stronger English listening and discussion with visual/context support than independent academic reading and written explanations. English development differs across tasks and domains. The language-access plan is available, but classroom implementation logs and the earlier school's instruction and intervention records have not yet been reviewed. These gaps do not establish whether inadequate instruction primarily explains the reading concern.

During an English science lesson, Marisol explains the concept using a diagram and partner discussion, but has difficulty independently reading the written directions. In a brief Spanish reading sample arranged by qualified bilingual staff, she hesitates on unfamiliar words; no age/grade comparison, systematic response-to-teaching record or comprehensive Spanish literacy assessment accompanies that sample. Her family requests an evaluation and participation through a qualified Spanish interpreter. The team has begun the evaluation process while language and reading supports continue.

An English-only assessment summary lists low reading performance but does not document the assessment's linguistic suitability, norming applicability, administration adaptations or interpretation limits. No standardized scores from that summary are supplied for this practice record. Vision/hearing screening reports, the complete medical history and a full review across the academic areas are also absent from the excerpt. The record raises a reading concern and an assessment-validity question; it establishes neither SLD nor a language-only explanation.
assumptions: All details are fictional. Schooling durations, service schedules and language descriptions are case context, not eligibility thresholds or required waiting periods.
The evaluation proceeds with appropriate procedures while ESOL, content-access and reading supports continue; Marisol does not have to reach an English-proficiency threshold before evaluation.

The English-only summary's suitability has not been established. Its omission from this score record is a validity safeguard, not a finding that all English assessments or all standardized assessments are unsuitable for multilingual learners.

The abbreviated record intentionally leaves appropriate-instruction verification, primary-cause analysis, assessment validity, SLD identification and any necessary special-education instruction unresolved. Family concerns and strengths remain relevant.
scoreGuidance: No interpretable standardized score record is supplied. The English-only summary's language/norming suitability and interpretation limits have not been established. Use the case observations to plan appropriate language/literacy, work-sample, classroom and instruction evidence; do not infer scores or repair validity by changing score formats. This does not mean all standardized assessments are unsuitable for multilingual learners.
evidencePrompt: Select case observations that matter to your evidence plan. Explain what is directly documented, what remains uncertain and which appropriate sources could clarify it. Your selected roles are discussion judgments, not findings of SLD or of a language-only cause.

scoreRecordMetadata.comparison: No interpretable standardized score record supplied
scoreRecordMetadata.note: Use the case observations and identify appropriate evidence to obtain; do not infer scores, percentiles or confidence intervals.

tasks.prompt: Separate Marisol's documented strengths and reading concerns from assumptions about language development or disability. Which records would clarify appropriate instruction and access?
Explain why the English-only summary and brief Spanish sample do not settle the form. Plan culturally and linguistically appropriate assessment with relevant language-acquisition expertise.
Identify evidence needed for Q3, especially Q3d, without treating multilingual status, an interruption in schooling or cross-language difficulty as an automatic answer.
Explain the current uncertainty to the family, name actionable evidence requests, and describe how evaluation and current supports can proceed together.

Q1.responseLabel: More evidence needed: achievement review incomplete
Q1.feedback: The excerpt does not provide multiple appropriate, valid sources establishing age and grade expectations across the academic areas. Reading concerns merit inquiry; neither an English-only summary nor one brief Spanish sample resolves Q1.

Q2.responseLabel: More evidence needed: instruction and access not fully verified
Q2.feedback: Review prior and current literacy teaching, language-development instruction, classroom language access and implementation. An interruption or missing log identifies a question to investigate; it does not establish the primary explanation for underachievement.

Q3.responseLabel: More evidence needed: verify every subpart
Q3.feedback: Gather evidence for each listed factor. Analyze Q3d using language/literacy history, appropriate instruction, family input and relevant assessment. Multilingual status or difficulty in both languages alone cannot establish or exclude SLD.

Q4.responseLabel: More evidence needed: appropriate pattern evidence incomplete
Q4.feedback: The record lacks sufficient appropriate evidence across intervention response, classroom performance, achievement and psychological processing. Do not convert differences between task conditions into an established SLD pattern.

Q5.responseLabel: Observation narrative with language and task context
Q5.feedback: Describe concept explanation with diagrams/partner support and difficulty reading written directions independently. Record the language, task, supports and observer qualifications; distinguish observation from a causal inference.

Q6.feedback: Record that relevant medical and vision/hearing information has not been supplied, then seek appropriate records. Absence from this excerpt is not verification that every relevant finding is absent.

Q7.responseLabel: More evidence needed: linguistic validity and qualifications review
Q7.feedback: Review purpose, administration, language suitability, norms, adaptations, interpretation limits and qualified personnel. Use the child's native language or communication mode unless clearly infeasible. Appropriate work/performance evidence is needed where relevant norms are unavailable; converting a score format does not repair validity.

Q8.responseLabel: SLD conclusion unresolved in this practice excerpt
Q8.feedback: Complete the appropriate evaluation and instruction/primary-cause review before making the supported team conclusion. Uncertainty calls for timely evidence gathering, not a language-proficiency waiting rule or an automatic SLD or language-only verdict.

Q9.responseLabel: Instruction-need decision unresolved; Q8 not established
Q9.feedback: Q9 follows a supported Q8 YES conclusion. This planning exercise does not settle that premise or whether general education can adequately meet the need. Identify necessary supports and evidence to investigate; if eligible, ESOL and special education can both be provided.

debrief.summary: The useful outcome is a defensible evidence plan, not a forced eligibility answer. The record raises reading, instructional-access and assessment-validity concerns, while leaving their causes and any necessary specially designed instruction unresolved.
debrief.q9Example: We cannot yet select a supported Q9 option because SLD identification and the necessary instruction remain unresolved. We will gather appropriate language/literacy, instruction, assessment and classroom evidence while providing current supports and conducting the evaluation.
debrief.familyExplanation: Your observations and Marisol's strengths are important. We need a fuller picture of her reading and learning in the languages she uses, and of the instruction and supports she has received. We will work with language-acquisition and evaluation specialists and a qualified interpreter, continue supports, and evaluate without waiting for a particular English-proficiency level.
debrief.caution: Do not assume disability because reading is difficult in two languages, or assume language alone explains the concern because Marisol is multilingual. Schooling history and language development require evidence-based interpretation. No score or prescribed waiting period is inferred here.
nextEvidence: Prior and current literacy-instruction records and implementation of classroom language-access supports.
Family/student language and literacy history, obtained with qualified interpretation as needed.
Appropriate language/literacy assessment, supported work samples, task-context observations and response-to-teaching evidence with interpretation limits documented.
Relevant vision/hearing/medical information and verification of all Q3 subparts.

title: Taylor, Grade 5: progress and the instruction it requires
practiceFocus: Independent reading, supported progress and teaching adaptations
languageContext: English-language instruction; assessments appropriate for this fictional learner
narrative: Taylor is age 10 years, 7 months, in Grade 5 and receives reading instruction under an IEP. A comprehensive reevaluation includes appropriate achievement and psychological-processing assessments, repeated progress measures, classroom observations, work samples and student/family input. The qualified evaluators document a relevant pattern across the required evidence streams and continuing SLD affecting basic reading and reading fluency. Appropriate core instruction, intervention implementation and a documented review of each primary-cause factor are verified.

Taylor contributes thoughtful ideas to class discussion and meets many science and social-studies assignment expectations with accessible audio/text, previewed vocabulary and extra reading time. Independent unfamiliar-word reading and connected-text fluency remain below age and Grade 5 expectations across valid assessment, classroom work and repeated reading measures. Successful supported content work does not show adequate independent achievement in every academic area.

Taylor's progress measures show improvement during explicitly sequenced decoding instruction: smaller teaching steps, carefully selected word patterns, cumulative practice, immediate corrective feedback and flexible pacing adjusted from ongoing error analysis. Implementation and longitudinal transfer records document that these adaptations address Taylor's disability-related learning needs. Appropriate general education interventions and accommodations have not adequately addressed those needs without the specified teaching adaptations. The full reevaluation establishes that the adaptations remain necessary for access to and progress in the curriculum.

The family asks whether better report-card grades mean that the reading instruction can end. The team has not withdrawn necessary instruction to test that idea. It reviews existing instruction, implementation, independent performance, supported performance and generalization data. No educationally relevant medical finding is reported in the complete reviewed record. The few simulated scores below illustrate that record; they do not determine eligibility, calculate composites or replace the full evaluation.
assumptions: All details and score values are fictional. The abbreviated rows are generic age-based standard scores (mean 100, SD 15), not a branded battery or required assessment list; no percentile or confidence interval is supplied.

The full reevaluation is stipulated to be appropriate, valid, reliable and comprehensive, with qualified personnel, verified appropriate instruction and evidence for every Q3 subpart; no listed factor is the primary cause.

The full reviewed record establishes continuing SLD and the necessity of the specified disability-related adaptations; general education interventions/accommodations alone have not adequately met the need. Progress depends on the necessary instruction, rather than proving it unnecessary.

Success with content-access supports is distinguished from independent basic-reading/fluency achievement. No support-withdrawal trial, particular program, staff title, setting or score cutoff is required or used as the sole basis for the practice conclusion.
scoreGuidance: These four generic simulated achievement standard scores use mean 100, SD 15 and age-based comparisons. They are not a branded assessment battery, computed composites, required tests or eligibility cutoffs. Grade-level achievement and the need for instruction are established by the separate stipulated full record. No percentiles or confidence intervals are supplied or inferred.
evidencePrompt: Select findings that help distinguish independent reading from supported content performance, and explain how the full-record assumptions affect your reasoning. Relate teaching adaptations to the documented learning needs; no particular number or selection of findings is required.

tasks.prompt: Separate successful content access from independent basic-reading and fluency achievement. Which sources inform Q1, and what would passing grades leave unexplained?
Distinguish audio/text access supports from the specified teaching adaptations. Explain their purposes using the case record rather than a program, setting or staff title.
Use the full-record assumptions to explain Q8 and Q9 separately. Why does improvement under necessary instruction not by itself establish general education sufficiency?
Explain the recommendation to the family and identify the implementation, independent-performance and transfer evidence that should continue to inform instructional planning.

Q1.feedback: The complete valid record identifies inadequate independent basic reading and fluency for age and grade expectations. Supported content success or passing grades does not establish the Q1 YES premise across every academic area.

Q2.feedback: The stipulated full record verifies appropriate core instruction, qualified delivery and implementation. Underachievement is not attributed to lack of appropriate instruction; continue through the form using that documented basis.

Q3.responseLabel: All subparts NO under the full-record assumptions
Q3.feedback: The complete review includes supporting evidence for each listed factor and finds none is the primary cause. This is an exercise assumption, not a result inferred merely from the four score rows.

Q4.responseLabel: YES: relevant pattern established by the full record
Q4.feedback: The reevaluation stipulates a relevant pattern from intervention response, classroom, achievement and psychological-processing evidence. Relate independent reading weakness, supported content strengths and necessary teaching adaptations without treating one score difference as the decision.

Q5.responseLabel: Observation narrative: task and support conditions
Q5.feedback: Describe strong oral/content participation with access supports alongside independent reading errors/slow fluency. Link observed behavior to the academic difficulty and identify the supports present; do not substitute assignment grades for observation.

Q6.responseLabel: No relevant medical finding reported in the reviewed record
Q6.feedback: Record the full record's report that no educationally relevant medical finding is identified. Q6 remains a narrative field rather than a YES/NO eligibility checkbox.

Q7.responseLabel: YES under the documented validity/qualification assumptions
Q7.feedback: Appropriate, valid/reliable assessment and qualified evaluation are stipulated in the comprehensive record. The generic score excerpt alone would not establish those assurances in an actual evaluation.

Q8.responseLabel: YES: continuing SLD established by the full reevaluation
Q8.feedback: The exercise expressly establishes continuing SLD through the complete review. State that basis separately from Q9; neither better grades nor the isolated score rows replace the supported team conclusion.

Q9.feedback: The full record establishes that disability-related adaptations to methodology/delivery remain necessary and that general education interventions/accommodations alone have not adequately met the need. Improvement while receiving that necessary instruction does not establish that it is unnecessary.

debrief.summary: Q1 NO and Q8 YES follow the complete stipulated record; Q9a is supported by the documented necessity of the teaching adaptations. Successful supported content work and progress are compatible with continuing special-education need.
debrief.q9Example: Taylor's SLD continues to limit independent basic reading and fluency despite appropriate instruction. The full record shows that specifically sequenced teaching, corrective feedback and individualized pacing remain necessary to address those disability-related needs, while general education interventions/accommodations alone are insufficient; Q9a is supported.
debrief.familyExplanation: Taylor's progress matters, and the record connects that improvement to the instruction and access supports Taylor is receiving. Reading independently remains difficult. We will continue the necessary teaching adaptations and review progress, implementation and transfer evidence; better grades alone do not show that the reading instruction can end.
debrief.caution: Describe the adaptation, the disability-related need and the evidence of necessity. Individualization, intensity, a branded program, staff title or location alone does not define SDI. Do not withdraw necessary support simply to demonstrate dependence.
nextEvidence: Continued implementation and error-analysis records for the necessary teaching adaptations.
